memory_candidates.content: A repo's shared build-guard wrapper can silently no-op: `lake-build-guard.sh build --timeout 1800 --` with NO lake args after the `--` exits 77 (usage error) and prints help, and if the call is piped through `tail`, the pipeline still reports exit 0. Four phases of 'green builds' were actually usage errors before this was caught. The correct form passes the lake subcommand after the separator: `-- build`, `-- build BimodalTest`, `-- exe runLinter FormalSystem`. When a wrapper script guards an expensive operation, assert on a positive success marker in its output (here: 'Build completed successfully (N jobs)'), never on the pipeline's exit code alone.

Large Lean identifier renames must be planned leaf-first (derived statements -> validity predicates -> frame predicates -> the inductive constructors last), because renaming a constructor first breaks every dependent file at once and leaves no green intermediate state. Equally important: enumerate the coupled NON-Lean artifacts that hardcode fully-qualified declaration names before planning phases, and pin each one to the phase that breaks it. In this repo those are check-module-invariants.sh's C14 axiom baselines AND its matched `#print axioms` probe block (both must move together, and a name renamed in a later phase must NOT be moved early or C14 fails in the earlier phase), typst-status-counts.sh's greps into a def body (which silently return 0 after a rename), the byte-for-byte-compared typst/generated/ artifacts, round-trip string parser/emitter pairs in Automation/, and scripts/nolints.json docBlame grandfather entries (hand-edit, never regenerate). A rename that only builds green has not been verified.

When a repo-wide gate script is slow (BimodalLogic's check-module-invariants.sh takes ~40 min cold: it runs `lake build`, `lake build BimodalTest`, and `lake exe runLinter`), extract its individual expensive checks into standalone scratch re-runs for per-phase verification and reserve the full script for the phases whose Verification Tier is 'full'. The C14 axiom-probe half in particular can be re-run alone in ~1 min by awk-extracting the script's own C14BASE and C14LEAN heredocs and diffing `lake env lean` output against the baseline -- this catches a renamed-but-not-rebuilt declaration ('Unknown constant') that a plain `lake build` cannot, because the probe file is not part of any build target.

A word can carry two senses in one codebase, and a global rename destroys the sense you did not mean. In BimodalLogic 'Discrete'/'Dedekind' named both a FrameClass tag (rename target) and the paper's bare order conditions plus the Dedekind-INF/SUP API (560 occurrences, must not move). The defense that worked: a KEEP-list guard script asserting exact expected counts for each protected family, run after every phase, plus word-boundary- and dot-anchored substitutions (`s/\.Discrete\b/.ZTime/g`) rather than bare `s/Discrete/ZTime/g`. Before the atomic pass, a qualifier survey (`grep -rhoE '[A-Za-z_.]*\.(Discrete|Dedekind)\b' | sort -u`) confirmed the only qualifier was `FrameClass.`, which is what makes the anchored sed safe. When a guard count legitimately moves (prose added a reference), verify the DECLARATIONS are unmoved rather than rebaselining blindly.
